# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot feel any useful information from the bomb yet. I need the manual’s rule from Mute, and Deaf must inspect the display, light, and wire markings and report those visual facts to Mute. I am defining the waving gesture as the request to report all visible bomb details.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me its complete cutting rule next turn. Also gesture 👋 to Deaf, meaning: inspect and report every visible detail of the display, light, and wires aloud to you.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signalled this gesture sequence: ? ? ? ? ? ? ? ?. Its meaning is not established yet.

Deaf has provided the bomb’s visible state: display 0, white light, and wires yellow, green, blue in positions 1–3. The cutting rule is still unknown because Mute’s gesture was not readable to me. I am asking Mute to state the manual’s rule plainly; no wire is safe to cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's complete rule to me plainly, including which wire position to cut for display 0, white light, and wire colors yellow, green, blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Updated bomb view: display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signalled a waving-hand gesture, then victory sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, OK sign, index-up gesture. I do not know their meaning; please use the manual and tell me what action is required.

The visual state has changed: the light is now purple, while the display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, green, blue. I still do not have the manual’s rule, so I must not act on the wire. Mute can read the manual and should combine it with these observations, then tell me the exact wire position to cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current bomb state: display 0; light purple; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Use the manual to determine the exact position to cut and tell me plainly as soon as possible.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current bomb view: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's latest signs, in order, are: victory sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, OK sign, index-up sign, OK sign, index-up sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, index-up sign. Treat this as an exact gesture sequence, not an interpreted instruction.

The latest sequence has no established meaning, so it cannot safely identify a wire. I will establish an unambiguous code through speech: Mute should use exactly one gesture for the wire position selected by the manual, based on the current bomb state. Deaf can then report that single gesture to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Establishing a code now: after applying the manual to the latest bomb state, gesture exactly one symbol for the required wire position: ✊ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 👌 means position 3. Do not send any other gestures. Use the current state, display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 4: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's new signal is one gesture: ?, the victory-sign gesture. No meaning has been established.

Deaf reports that Mute sent the victory-sign gesture, which under the code I proposed means wire position 2. However, the code was not acknowledged by Mute, and the bomb state changed to white light, so I should not assume that signal is a valid answer. I need Mute to state the manual’s rule and the resulting position in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not gesture. Speak the manual's rule and the exact required wire position in plain words for the current state: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5: display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's new signal is one gesture: ?, the OK-sign gesture.

The OK gesture reported now is Mute’s response to my previous request, but it corresponds to the prior state (white light), not necessarily the current purple-light state. I will ask Mute to apply the same one-gesture position code to the current state and will wait for Deaf to relay it; no cut is yet justified.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state now, display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue: apply the manual and send exactly one gesture using our code: ✊ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 👌 means position 3. Send no other gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 6: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. No new gesture from Mute this turn. Please report the manual's required action or your current status.

I still do not know the manual’s rule or a confirmed wire position. The changing light means earlier gesture reports cannot safely be reused. Mute can reach me directly by speech, so I am requesting the exact rule and answer in words rather than another gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer me in words, not gestures: what does the manual require for display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue? State only the exact wire position to cut, or state that the rule requires waiting.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 7: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's new signal is one gesture: ?, the victory-sign gesture.

Mute’s latest victory-sign response is for the latest reported state: display 0, white light, and wires yellow, green, blue. Under the position code I established, the victory sign means position 2. This is the first consistent position signal tied to the current reported state, so I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
